located_source.title: Plasma p-tau181 as a promising non-invasive biomarker of Alzheimer's Disease pathology in Subjective Cognitive Decline and Mild Cognitive Impairment
located_source.citation: Giacomucci G, Mazzeo S, Crucitti C, et al. Journal of the Neurological Sciences 453 (2023) 120805, doi:10.1016/j.jns.2023.120805

is_model_study_note: single-marker ROC/Youden cut-point (plasma p-tau181, AUC 0.910) evaluated in-sample on 58 SCD+MCI patients
blind_first: blind codes were written to this file before the registry codes file was opened

blind_codes.Task_Type: T4 (biomarker study; its ROC cut-point discriminates AD-pathology carriers vs non-carriers among SCD+MCI, not MCI vs HC; T1 arguable)
blind_codes.Validation_Type: V2 (in-sample ROC/Youden cut-point, no CV or test set)
blind_codes.Sample_N: 79 (33 SCD + 32 MCI + 14 AD dementia); 72 with CSF; ROC on 58 SCD+MCI

registry_codes.Sample_N_Approx: 79 patients (33 SCD, 32 MCI, 14 AD-d); 72 with CSF

Task_Type.reason: Two readings. T1 under the deciding test: a cut-point is evaluated and discrimination is quantified (AUC 0.910, cut-off 2.69 pg/mL, sensitivity/specificity/PPV/NPV), and the test says HC existence is not the criterion. T4: the discriminated classes are CSF/PET-defined AD-pathology carriers vs non-carriers among pooled SCD+MCI patients; the study has no healthy-control group ('the lack of a healthy control group', p. 7) and no MCI-vs-HC contrast, so it is a fluid-biomarker study. My blind code was T4. For the census, keeping T1 counts this row as an 'MCI vs HC discrimination' study although it contains no HC group.
Task_Type.quote: we merged SCD and MCI, as there were no differences between these groups in p-tau181 concentrations when adjusted for confounding variables. The analysis showed that plasma p-tau181 was highly accurate for discriminating between AP+ and AP- patients (AUC = 0.910)

Category.reason: Plasma p-tau181 (SiMoA), CSF Abeta42, Abeta42/40, p-tau, t-tau (Lumipulse), APOE genotyping. Amyloid PET in 18 patients only is marginal.

Validation_Type.reason: V1 requires leave-one-out cross-validation. The paper derives the Youden-optimal cut-off and reports its accuracy on the same patients, with no cross-validation of any kind (full text searched: no leave-one-out, k-fold, bootstrap, test set or external cohort). Small n alone does not make V1; absent validation is V2 under the definitions.
Validation_Type.quote: Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were performed to evaluate the ability of plasma p-tau181 to distinguish between AP+ and AP- patients. The Youden's method was used to detect the best cut-off value and accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value and negative predictive value for plasma p-tau181.

Sample_N_Approx.reason: 79 patients (33 SCD, 32 MCI, 14 AD dementia) with plasma; 72 (26 SCD, 32 MCI, 14 AD-d) with CSF (p. 2).

Publication_Year.reason: Journal of the Neurological Sciences 453 (2023) 120805; available online 12 September 2023.

ADNI_Dependent.reason: Consecutive patients of the Careggi Hospital memory clinic, Florence; ADNI not used.
